question: On 20 November 2025, the Municipality of Torri del Benaco (Province of Verona) adopted a development plan (P.I. 3.1) which provides for further expansion and land take in an area that is saturated with tourism and speculative development and includes two sites of Community importance (SCIs)1. The development plan identifies measures for the transformation of the area in line with the local land-use plan (PAT).

The current PAT2 is subject to specific environmental requirements, such as ‘environmental improvement with a view to strengthening or enhancing landscape features of primary importance for species of Community interest, taking account of ecological and functional connectivity with areas of the Natura 2000 network3’.

It is crucial, therefore, that the plan’s cumulative effects on the environment and land use are looked into. However, of the roughly 320 building works provided for in P.I. 3, only 50 were included in P.I. 3.14, which suggests that attempts are being made to bypass the strategic environmental assessment (SEA) or its screening procedure.

In the light of the above, and to prevent the carving up of this excessive development and ensure that the overall environmental impacts of Torri del Benaco town planning instruments are properly assessed, could the Commission investigate whether the SEA legislation has been complied with?

IT3210007 – Monte Baldo: Val dei Mulini, Senge di Marciaga, Rocca di Garda; IT3210004 – Monte Luppia and Punta San Vigilio. 2 Amendment 2, approved by the Province of Verona on 19 June 2025. 3 Veneto Region, technical appraisal report 85/2023 for the SEA impact assessment for amendment 2 to the PAT of the Municipality of Torri del Benaco, 27 April 2023. 4 P.I. 3.

1 was definitively approved by the Municipal Council on 29 April 2026, rejecting numerous comments submitted within the framework of the public consultation procedure, including that of the Legal Intervention Group (GrIG),which complained about the artificial fragmentation of land. In the counterarguments prepared by the Municipality of Torri del Benaco, the issue of fragmentation was simply ignored.
In the meantime, the municipality is working on a new urban planning amendment that increases land take. 1
answer: According to Article 3 of the Strategic Environmental Assessment Directive (SEAD) (1), an environmental assessment shall be carried out for plans and programmes which are likely to have significant environmental effects. This includes plans and programmes which are prepared for tourism or land use and plans or programmes that have been determined to require an assessment pursuant to the Habitats Directive (2).

Moreover, based on Article 3 (4) of SEAD, Member States shall determine whether plans and programmes that set the framework for future development consent of projects are likely to have significant environmental effects.

It would seem that the planning instrument referred to would set the framework for future projects listed in Annex II of the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive (3), namely apartment projects (depending on their size and scale) and could be covered by point 10(b) of Annex II and be subject to a screening.

As pointed out by the Honourable Member, it would seem that there was an assessment procedure carried out, including public consultation. Furthermore, it seems that the municipality is in the process of preparing a new urban planning amendment and might still opt for further screening and/or environmental assessment as appropriate.
Therefore, at this stage, the Commission cannot establish that there is a breach of EU law.

Furthermore, without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible to ensure compliance with EU law, including verifying individual cases of potential breach of the relevant rules. In line with its strategic approach on enforcement action (4) the Commission focuses on systemic non-compliance.
